messages.subject: Printing hyperlinks
parts:
Hello everyone!

I've been looking for this in google but didn't find it, maybe you can help me. I'm doing an analysis report in knitr and my data frame contains an attribute that is an URL to a WebPage.

What I'm trying to accomplish is: The printed output of each chunk of code in the HTML version to have the URL attribute like a link, so the user can easily navigate to those URLs when reviewing the report.

Is there a way to achieve this? I now that the markdown is [name](url), but what I'm trying is that the output of the chunk to be rendered as a link.

Use Case:
I have a dataframe containing "Website URL" and "Anual Visitors", If I print the top 10 most visited webpages, I want the output to have a clickable link to the site.

Thanks a lot!

Regards,

P.S: Is there a way for the url's to be clickable in RStudio console?

messages.author: 3952bd5e6cb8248a
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Printing hyperlinks
parts:
Here is something that works for me:

library(dplyr)
url <- c("http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com",
         "http://www.google.com")
sitename <- c("RMarkdown",
              "Google")
Visitors <- c(200,10000)
d <- data.frame(sitename,url,Visitors) %>%
  mutate(Sites = paste0("[", sitename, "](", url, ")")) %>%
  select(Sites, Visitors) %>%
  arrange(Visitors %>% desc)
rownames(d) <- paste0(1:nrow(d),".")
knitr::kable(d)
